key_findings: The coarse mesh (3,923 elements) solves in 41m 39s on HPC (Job 1421286) but completely fails to resolve the secondary process zone (0.00% <= l0).
The standard uniform fine PFM requires ~86,000 elements to guarantee h <= l0/2 everywhere, with estimated serial solve time of ~14h.
The single-frame native remeshed mesh (9,568 elements) achieves 88.87% element savings but suffers from primary corridor relaxation (0.00% <= l0/2).

The two-branch history-aware mesh (18,984 elements, e_tgt=2.5%) achieves improved dual-corridor localization (h_min = 0.0513 mm <= l0/5) while still reducing element count by 77.93% relative to uniform fine discretization.
Tightening errorTarget to 2.5% is classified as a modified-method sensitivity experiment rather than direct reproduction of the published 5.0% setting.
